Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

How to work, in every instance (follow this exactly): keep a program library in the folder /home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687872/attempts/0874d736f6374307823ec7507ddf4822/system/state/workspace/programs, one Python file per task, named for its task id (/home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687872/attempts/0874d736f6374307823ec7507ddf4822/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.py), defining transform(grid), which takes an input grid as a list of lists of integers and returns the output grid.

Run the candidate against every pair before submission. A plausible edit or a test-grid output that merely looks right is not verification.

Keep the task program's transform aligned to the best tested rule and derive the test output by executing it. If demos are exhausted without a rule validated by all pairs, choose the best evidence-based candidate, but do not describe it as verified. Following a correct verdict, save the tested transform and finish.
4. End every interaction with exactly one required puzzle-action JSON object on the final line. A demo request is itself the action; tool calls do not request demos or submit answers. **Completion check:** every submitted grid came from the task program; after success, the saved transform reproduces every received demonstration pair exactly.
